title: Provide a completion bridge for sandboxed Agy workflows
description:
Historical isolation finding from the 2026-09-07 hcom-f6g.12 run: the then-current user-created hcom run agy workflow explicitly launched Antigravity with --sandbox, while ordinary hcom agy did not. Antigravity provider-native sandbox failed and the safe proceed-in-sandbox policy denied command execution rather than permitting a host bypass, so the worker could not run its prompt-mandated hcom send completion command. The forced --sandbox flag was removed from the user workflow on 2026-09-08; this issue now applies only to the future hcom-owned isolated-workspace rollout and is not a current ordinary run-agy defect.

## Steps to Reproduce
Historical only until the hcom-owned isolation runtime exists: launch an Agy workflow inside the approved isolation boundary, complete useful work while ordinary provider shell execution is unavailable, and verify whether the outer coordinator can still receive an authoritative attempt-bound result without terminal intervention. Do not re-enable the removed provider-native --sandbox flag to reproduce this.
acceptance_criteria: Before isolated Agy workflows are enabled for daily use, their hcom result path remains available inside the approved isolation boundary or is published by the outer coordinator without requiring a provider shell command. A sandbox failure remains fail-closed, never requests or grants host bypass, and returns a typed incomplete-turn or recovery outcome. Deterministic result-bridge tests and an isolated live Antigravity run pass without terminal injection.
notes: Difficulty assessment 2026-09-08: not a standalone current run-agy repair after removal of the forced provider sandbox. It belongs to the future hcom-owned isolation rollout, primarily OpenSpec tasks 5.1-5.2 and 6.2-6.3, and depends on hcom-f6g.3/hcom-f6g.4 infrastructure. Implementation crosses private workflow state, result correlation, PTY/runtime boundary, provider adapter policy, cleanup ordering, and containment/live tests; treat as hard security-sensitive integration work and split along the existing OpenSpec task boundaries.

title: Resume Antigravity delivery after an approval denial
description: During the 2026-09-07 hcom-f6g.12 Agy implementation run, denying Antigravity's sandbox-bypass dialog cleared the provider prompt but left hcom lifecycle state stale. A targeted hcom send was persisted yet did not schedule a new turn, forcing direct PTY prompt injection. This is the Antigravity counterpart to the Claude-specific denial recovery proven under tracker item 36.
acceptance_criteria: After any recognized Antigravity approval denial, hcom detects the settled actionable prompt, transitions the matching generation out of blocked/active state, and schedules exactly one already-queued targeted delivery without direct PTY injection. Newer provider transitions and still-visible approval menus remain protected; deterministic tests and one live run pass.
notes: Difficulty assessment 2026-09-08: likely superseded by hcom-f6g.12 rather than an independent implementation bug. The observed failure used the pre-fix binary, which never classified the approval, so injected denial had no PTY approval state to clear. Current code synchronously clears recognized injected approvals to listening and the focused sandbox-bypass falling-edge plus clear-injection tests pass. Do not implement speculatively; first run one targeted live denial-and-queued-follow-up reproduction. If it still fails, expected patch scope is narrow-to-medium in src/pty/shared.rs/screen.rs plus delivery integration tests.
close_reason: Live verification with the freshly built f6g.12 code proved no independent bug remains. A raw Gemini 3.8 Flash High worker entered blocked/pty:approval for an outside-workspace file request; a targeted follow-up was queued while blocked; denying option 3 published pty:approval_cleared and listening; delivery then transitioned the same generation to active and the worker returned F6G13_RESUMED without direct PTY prompt injection. Focused approval falling-edge and injected-clear tests pass. The earlier failure used the pre-f6g.12 binary, which had never classified the approval.

title: Detect Antigravity sandbox-bypass approval prompts
description: During the 2026-09-06 hcom-f6g.11 live Claude Opus run, Antigravity reported a sandbox connection issue and displayed an approval dialog asking to bypass the sandbox for a harmless bd show command. hcom continued publishing active/tool:run_command for more than 224 seconds instead of a typed blocker, leaving the high-level run wait silent until terminal inspection.
acceptance_criteria: The complete Antigravity sandbox-bypass permission dialog is recognized without matching ordinary task text; the instance transitions promptly to blocked/pty:approval with command/evidence preserved; a correlated --result-from wait returns the typed blocker without terminal inspection; denial/clearance returns lifecycle state correctly; deterministic screen/shared-state/event tests and one live reproduction pass without approving sandbox bypass.
close_reason: Implemented typed detection for complete Antigravity sandbox-bypass approval dialogs, preserved command evidence through shared lifecycle and result waits, verified denial/clearance, and live-tested Gemini 3.8 Flash High returning exit 4 without terminal inspection or approval input. Focused tests, cargo check, clippy, formatting, diff check, and review passed; broad suite remains at its known environment-dependent transcript PATH failure (2318 passed, 1 failed, 1 ignored).

title: Make result waits terminate on actionable worker blockers
description: A raw Antigravity launch batch reported ready, then the worker entered pty:approval immediately. The coordinator's hcom events --result-from wait remained silent because it watches only terminal results, so it could wait until the full task deadline while no work occurs. A separate blocked wait is race-prone when the transition occurs before its cursor is captured.
acceptance_criteria: One high-level or composable wait can atomically return the correlated workflow result, a typed actionable blocker, launch failure, stopped-without-result state, or deadline. It cannot miss a blocker between readiness and wait registration, and its structured outcome preserves worker generation, workflow thread, attempt cursor, blocker evidence, and recovery guidance.
notes: Live Antigravity Claude Opus attempt on 2026-09-06 did not reach code work. agy sandbox reported a connection issue on 'bd prime', retried 'bd show hcom-f6g.11', then requested permission to bypass the sandbox for that harmless read. hcom remained active/tool:run_command for over 224 seconds instead of surfacing pty:approval; the high-level wrapper stayed silent until the parent inspected the terminal and terminated the worker. No bypass was approved and no files were edited. This reproduces the result-or-blocker observability gap the issue must fix.
close_reason: Implemented one cursor-anchored correlated wait for exact result, typed blocker, launch failure, stopped-without-result, or deadline. Structured outcomes preserve generation/thread/cursor/evidence/recovery. Added race, resolution, generation-reuse, final-poll, payload, and CLI exit-code coverage. Focused tests, workspace check, strict Clippy, and two independent reviews passed; broad suite reached 2306 passed with two unrelated environment-dependent existing failures.

title: Schedule idle Antigravity turns after hcom delivery
description: A targeted hcom send to an idle Antigravity worker inserted the message into the TUI prompt and returned success, but left the worker in listening/tui:prompt-has-text without submitting the prompt. No active transition occurred within a bounded 60-second wait, requiring hcom term inject --enter.
acceptance_criteria: Targeted delivery to a supported idle Antigravity prompt either submits and schedules exactly one turn automatically, or returns an explicit non-actionable delivery state/blocker; successful send output cannot leave prompt text indefinitely awaiting external Enter input.
notes: The underlying screen-parser failure is broader than a missing Enter: Antigravity was at a ready empty prompt, but hcom reported tui:prompt-has-text because it treated the visible accept-edits mode banner as input_text. Delivery therefore remained queued and even a standalone Enter did not submit the intended message. Regression coverage must include this exact banner.
close_reason: Fixed the Antigravity screen-parser false positive: the agy mode banners (accept-edits/plan/best-of-N) rendered on the empty prompt row are now recognized as placeholder text (exact-match plus wrapped-prefix match), so a ready idle prompt parses as empty instead of tui:prompt-has-text. Delivery then follows the existing inject->Enter->verify state machine and schedules exactly one turn automatically; the parser fix also restores phase-2 clear detection and submit-edge stamping after Enter. Added regression tests for the exact accept-edits banner (non-dim render, with/without ready footer), plan/best-of-N banners, wrapped narrow-pane prefix, head-only typed text staying input, banner-after-submit emptiness, update_delivery_state wiring incl. submit-edge stamping, and the gate passing on the banner-derived empty prompt. Focused tests, fmt --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets, and clippy -D warnings all pass; the 6 hooks::claude full-suite failures reproduce identically at clean HEAD (pre-existing environmental).

title: Detect and dismiss Antigravity feedback surveys
description: Antigravity can display its post-command CLI feedback survey (Good/Fine/Bad/Skip) during an unattended hcom worker run. hcom leaves the instance falsely active on the previous tool state, so result waits remain silent and work stops until terminal input is injected.
acceptance_criteria: The Antigravity integration recognizes the complete feedback-survey screen without false positives, classifies it as a typed non-task prompt, and applies an explicit safe policy (such as dismissing with Skip) or returns an actionable blocker; unattended result waits cannot remain silently stuck behind it.
close_reason: Implemented complete survey recognition, safe Skip dismissal, bounded typed pty:survey fallback, retry ownership handling, Unix/Windows integration, and regression tests. Independent fmt/check/clippy and focused tests passed; two code reviews found no remaining blocking issue.

title: Enable isolated Antigravity Gemini and Claude workflows
description: Implement the provider capability and Antigravity adapter in OpenSpec tasks 6.1-6.4, then run Gemini and Claude trusted-local live gates without native sandbox bypass.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter fixtures pass and both provider matrices demonstrate edit, build/test, completion, cancellation, cleanup, and fresh-worktree startup inside the hcom boundary; failures remain preview-only and fail closed.

title: Add workflow-scoped hcom state and result bridge
description: Implement OpenSpec task group 5 using explicit WorkflowId and AttemptId tenancy, private HCOM_DIR state, correlated high-level results, and bounded worker/reviewer messaging.
acceptance_criteria: Tasks 5.1-5.3 pass; isolated participants cannot access global or unrelated workflow state; one blocking high-level wait returns the correct authoritative result.

title: Implement Bubblewrap runtime and fake-provider containment
description: Implement OpenSpec task groups 3 and 4 at the PTY provider-child seam, including canonical workspace/Git mounts, runtime ownership, fail-closed startup, and hermetic fake-provider containment.
acceptance_criteria: Tasks 3.1-4.4 pass; workspace operations succeed; outside writes, protected reads, disallowed Git mutations, host PID visibility, and unrestricted fallback are prevented; cleanup ordering is proven.

title: Upgrade Bubblewrap to a supported release
description: Make Bubblewrap 0.12.0 or newer available in the supported NixOS development and test environment. The installed 0.11.2 contains a sandbox-setup issue fixed by 0.12.0 and must remain rejected.
acceptance_criteria: hcom resolves Bubblewrap >=0.12.0, the binary has the expected ownership/capability posture, and the doctor namespace probe passes on NixOS.

title: Define isolation identity, configuration, and preflight
description: Implement OpenSpec task groups 1 and 2: isolation/workflow identity, launch metadata, CLI configuration, Linux/NixOS runtime discovery, authoritative Bubblewrap checks, doctor, and explain.
acceptance_criteria: Tasks 1.1-2.3 in the linked OpenSpec change are complete with deterministic tests; unsafe or unsupported hosts fail before provider launch; no secrets appear in plans.
notes: OpenSpec task 1.1 completed and parent-verified on 2026-09-06: 12 focused tests, cargo fmt --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets, and strict workspace Clippy pass. Raw Antigravity trial uncovered follow-ups hcom-f6g.9 (feedback survey blocker) and hcom-f6g.10 (idle delivery/prompt-text detection). Tasks 1.2-2.3 remain.

title: Add provider-neutral isolated worker workspaces
description: Unattended hcom workers are blocked by provider workspace-trust, exact-command approval, and unreliable provider-native sandbox behavior. Add a fail-closed hcom-owned isolation boundary for PTY-backed delegated workflows, beginning with Antigravity and Claude-backed GLM on Linux/NixOS. The architectural rationale is documented in docs/isolated-worker-workspaces.md.
design: Use an hcom IsolationProfile and serializable IsolationPlan, enforce through a Bubblewrap backend at the PTY provider-child spawn seam, retain the PTY supervisor outside, scope hcom state per workflow/attempt, keep Git metadata read-only by default, and never fall back to unrestricted host execution. Preserve the single-binary/local-SQLite architecture.
acceptance_criteria: OpenSpec artifacts define observable requirements and phased tasks; hcom can diagnose and explain an isolation plan; Bubblewrap preflight rejects unsafe/unsupported versions; fake-provider containment proves workspace writes and host denials; PTY-backed Antigravity and Claude/GLM runs complete without routine provider approvals; isolation failures are typed and fail closed; untrusted workloads remain disabled until credentials and egress are brokered.
notes:
Planning source: openspec/changes/add-isolated-worker-workspaces/. Current external blocker: the host Bubblewrap 0.11.2 must be upgraded to >=0.12.0 before containment work may pass its authoritative preflight. The trusted-local milestone permits visibly reported host networking; untrusted workloads remain deferred to child hcom-f6g.8.
Raw Gemini 3.8 Flash task 1.1 trial exposed three P0 prerequisites before further delegated implementation: hcom-f6g.9 feedback-survey handling, hcom-f6g.10 idle-turn delivery and false prompt-text detection, and hcom-f6g.11 atomic result-or-blocker waits. The OpenSpec change now requires risk-based permissions: routine in-boundary work and granted GitHub participation are non-interactive; boundary escape, protected resources, credential/policy changes, and ungranted destructive capabilities remain blocked.

title: Default raw Claude launches to auto permission mode
description:
Raw hcom claude launches currently pass no --permission-mode when HCOM_CLAUDE_ARGS is unset, so Claude Code defaults to manual and blocks delegated work on harmless commands such as bd show. The earlier hcom run glm fix applies auto only inside that user workflow and leaves the first-class Claude launcher inconsistent.

## Steps to Reproduce
With claude_args unset, launch hcom claude headless with a task that runs bd show. Observe Claude entering an approval blocker for the read-only command.
acceptance_criteria: hcom claude and Claude PTY launches default to --permission-mode auto; an explicit permission mode supplied through claude_args or CLI overrides the default without duplicate ambiguity; launch preview/help and focused argument-merging tests reflect the behavior; a live raw hcom claude worker executes bd show without an approval prompt.
close_reason: Raw Claude and Claude PTY launches now default to --permission-mode auto unless config or CLI supplies an explicit mode. Focused argument tests, workspace check, help/docs, and a live raw hcom claude bd show run passed without approval.

title: Preserve successful GLM results across provider-run cleanup races
description:
Tracker item 45: a live hcom run glm received an authoritative correlated result, then exited nonzero because cleanup of its temporary provider-runs directory raced another writer and returned Directory not empty. The current user workflow contains transcript-preserving and stale-run cleanup logic, but the original concurrent-cleanup failure has not been closed with a deterministic or live regression.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run the GLM workflow to a successful correlated completion while a provider process or transcript writer still touches the per-run profile directory during cleanup. The observed failure returned the valid result first, then failed the wrapper when recursive cleanup encountered Directory not empty.
acceptance_criteria: After an authoritative result is captured, bounded cleanup races cannot turn the workflow into failure; recoverable cleanup problems are structured warnings; genuine leaked processes or credential-bearing state still fail visibly with exact ownership/path; concurrent-writer and transcript-retention tests plus one live GLM completion/cleanup run pass.

title: Return a typed Antigravity workspace-trust blocker
description:
Tracker item 15: Antigravity has previously remained alive behind a workspace-trust screen, requiring terminal inspection. Generic launch-blocker classification now recognizes distinctive trust wording, but the Antigravity path and exact live screen have not been proven end to end. This fix must only surface the provider decision; it must not approve trust, inject confirmation keys, or mutate provider trust state.

## Steps to Reproduce
Launch Antigravity through hcom in a fresh workspace that Antigravity has not trusted. Leave the trust decision unanswered. Observe whether hcom promptly publishes a workspace_trust launch blocker with the prompt evidence or continues reporting an apparently live/launching worker.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic Antigravity workspace-trust fixture and one fresh untrusted-workspace live run publish a correlated launch blocker with blocked_kind=workspace_trust and exact evidence promptly; the high-level wait terminates actionably; ordinary task text mentioning workspace trust is rejected; no trust approval or provider state mutation occurs.

title: Use Claude auto permission mode for GLM workflow
description: The hcom GLM workflow hard-codes Claude Code acceptEdits, causing routine read/build/test and completion-report commands to stop for approval. Default the workflow to Claude auto mode, retain an explicit environment override for compatibility/testing, document the setting in workflow help, and live-test whether the Z.ai-backed Claude session accepts the mode.
acceptance_criteria: hcom run glm launches Claude with permission mode auto by default; an environment override can select another supported mode; help output documents the setting; shell validation and a live smoke test establish whether the installed Claude/Z.ai combination starts and executes a harmless command without an approval prompt.
notes: Verified after correcting this checkout from contributor to maintainer mode; the primary repository tracker is writable and contains the completed issue.
close_reason: GLM workflow now defaults to Claude auto mode and passed a live no-prompt smoke test.

title: Complete isolation observability and trusted-local rollout
description: Complete OpenSpec tasks 7.1-7.3: status/help/docs, all quality gates, provider support matrix, and deliberate default enablement for high-level trusted-local delegated workflows.
acceptance_criteria: All supported-platform quality and containment gates pass; effective policy is visible and secret-free; workspace becomes the delegated default only after every enabled provider gate succeeds; isolation never silently falls back.

title: Enable isolated GLM workflows
description: Implement the GLM provider adapter and OpenSpec task 6.5 after generic containment and workflow-scoped state are proven.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh-worktree GLM run passes edit/test/result, resume-invariant, cancellation, and cleanup gates without broad host access or routine permission prompts.

title: Remove remaining hcom command-grammar retry traps
description:
Tracker item 38: agents have attempted plausible forms such as transcript --tail, events --limit, SQL from_agent, and positional send syntax, causing extra help and retry calls. Some send compatibility has since improved, so this issue must first reproduce only the remaining traps and fix them additively without changing existing command semantics.

## Steps to Reproduce
Try each recorded form against the current CLI: hcom transcript NAME --tail N, hcom events --limit N, an events SQL filter using from_agent, and the formerly attempted positional send form. Record which are now accepted. For every remaining rejection, observe whether the error names the canonical equivalent such as --last, --from, or the documented send syntax.
acceptance_criteria: Each tracker example is covered by a CLI test; already-supported forms are documented as resolved; safe common aliases such as --tail/--limit either map to the canonical option or return the exact supported equivalent; SQL/filter errors identify the public field or flag to use; existing canonical syntax and exit behavior remain compatible.

title: Wake only resolved recipients after targeted sends
description:
Tracker item 29: the send path resolves an exact delivered_to set but still calls the system-wide wake_all helper, waking unrelated delivery loops for targeted and thread-resolved messages. This creates avoidable activity and notification work even though only declared recipients can consume the message.

## Steps to Reproduce
Register wake endpoints for at least two local agents, send a message targeted only to one agent, and observe that the send path calls wake_all and connects to both wake endpoints even though delivered_to contains only the intended recipient.
acceptance_criteria: Targeted and thread-resolved sends wake only their resolved local recipients and any explicitly required coordinator; explicit broadcasts retain fan-out; remote relay behavior remains correct; unavailable/stopped recipients remain safe; deterministic endpoint tests prove unrelated agents receive no wake while intended recipients still deliver promptly.

title: Harden isolation for untrusted and cross-workflow workloads
description: Follow-up scope from OpenSpec task 7.4: broker credentials and egress, authenticate narrow global/cross-workflow messaging, add other OS/native-print backends, and only then consider untrusted GitHub-event workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Host-network and ambient credential exposure are removed or strictly brokered, cross-workflow messaging is authenticated and scoped, supported backends have containment tests, and untrusted workloads are explicitly gated until all requirements pass.

title: Polish Antigravity survey blocker retry cadence
description: The verified hcom-f6g.9 survey dismissal path has two low-severity operational follow-ups: keep the Unix poll cap active while a failed pty:survey Unblock is pending so clearing does not fall back to the 10-second idle cadence, and rate-limit repeated pty.survey_block_deferred warnings when an instance remains unbound or another blocker owns the row.
acceptance_criteria: A pending survey unblock retries on the intended bounded cadence on Unix, repeated blocker-publication deferrals are rate-limited, and focused state-machine/logging tests pass.
